order: Fix the abandoned-worktree sweep in the disposable-checkout module. It recognizes its own leftovers by testing whether a registered worktree's path CONTAINS the module's temporary-directory prefix, then removes that worktree and recursively deletes its parent. Two reproductions have landed: CI deleted the OS temp root, because the fixture repository's name carried the prefix; and a delta re-review destroyed a legitimate worktree under a prefix-substring ancestor. Replace the substring test with a STRUCTURAL one — a leftover is exactly <tmp>/<prefix>XXXX/checkout, and only that immediate parent may be removed — skip the main worktree as a second belt, and keep the live-checkout exemption. Pin both reproducer shapes as regressions; record the re-review verdict verbatim and fold its dispositions into the round's ledger. IN SCOPE: the sweep function's identification and removal rule, those two regressions, those two roster documents. Constraints: leave every module-level constant and default exactly as the base has them, and change no behaviour outside the sweep's identification rule.
claims: Leftover identification is now structural rather than a substring test: a candidate qualifies only when its own basename is `checkout` and its immediate parent's basename carries the module's temporary-directory prefix, and only that parent is ever removed. The main worktree is skipped outright as a second belt, and the live-checkout exemption is unchanged. Both reproducer shapes are pinned as regressions, and the re-review verdict and its dispositions are recorded. Nothing outside the sweep's identification and removal rule was altered. Suites green: verifier 96, router 135, registry 31.
